title: Effects of audio-visual interactions on soundscape and landscape perception and their influence on satisfaction with the urban environment
research_question: This study investigated the relationship between overall satisfaction with the urban environment and its soundscape and landscape based on a subjective evaluation of the audio-visual interaction effects within various urban spaces with different environmental conditions.

participants.description: 20 male, 10 female university students from Hanyang University, Seoul, South Korea, aged 22-29 years (mean: 24.80, SD: 1.97). All had normal hearing.
participants.recruitment: Students from the authors' university (Hanyang University)

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Immersive virtual reality (VR) simulations of 9 urban evaluation locations (ELs) in Seoul, representing various urban contexts (e.g., roads, green areas, rivers, buildings). Visual information provided via head-mounted display (HMD) (VIVE Pro 2) with 8k ultra-high definition 360-degree videos. Audio information provided via open-type headphones (Sennheiser HD-650) using first-order ambisonics (FOA) with head-tracking technology for 3D auralization. Three experimental environments: audio-only, visual-only, and audio-visual.
stimuli_or_exposures.source: 2.1.1. Case study area, 2.1.2. Audio-visual recording, 2.1.3. VR soundscape environment reproduction, 2.2.2. Experimental setups

measures.instrument: 5-category classification system (traffic, human, bird, wind, music) with 5-point Likert preference scale ('Dislike (1)' to 'Like (5)')
7 visual elements (vehicle, building, road, open space, vegetation, people, sky) with 5-point Likert preference scale ('Dislike (1)' to 'Like (5)')
8 semantic attributes (pleasant, unpleasant, calm, chaotic, eventful, uneventful, exciting, monotonous) on a 7-point semantic differential scale
12 semantic attributes (comfortable, uncomfortable, harmonious, disharmonious, natural, artificial, open, closed, wide, narrow, orderly, disorderly) on a 7-point semantic differential scale

mechanisms: Multisensory integration and cross-modal congruency: Visual and auditory information interact to influence perception and preference, with congruent cues enhancing positive experiences and incongruent cues detracting from them.
Cognitive load and expectation violation: Unpleasant or unexpected stimuli (e.g., traffic noise) can increase cognitive load and negatively impact satisfaction.
Biophilic response: Natural elements and sounds (e.g., birdsong, vegetation) evoke positive affective responses and enhance perceived naturalness and overall quality.
Dominance of visual information: Visual cues play a more significant role in overall environmental satisfaction compared to auditory cues.
implementation_implications: The newly proposed audio-visual interaction-based satisfaction models can be used for better urban planning.
The findings provide effective and concrete guidelines to improve satisfaction levels in newly designed urban spaces.

limitations: The study used a limited number of evaluation locations (ELs) in which music was provided, potentially affecting the statistical significance of music-related findings.
The study was conducted with a relatively small and homogeneous sample of university students, which may limit the generalizability of the findings to other populations.
The study was conducted in a specific cultural context (Seoul, Korea), and results may differ in Eastern and Western countries with different urban densities and morphologies.
Virtual reality technology, while immersive, does not fully replicate all sensory experiences (e.g., haptic, olfactory, thermal) of actual urban environments.
